newsitem.title: USA: Senate chair sees "highway robbery" in funds bill.
newsitem.headline: Senate chair sees "highway robbery" in funds bill.

text.p: The chairman of a key U.S. Senate panel on Wednesday said that members of Congress from the Northeast are stealing U.S. highway dollars from states in the South, West and Midwest.

Sen. John Warner, R-Va., head of the Senate's transportation and infrastructure subcommittee, made the charge as the Senate this week debates how much supplemental federal highway funding to give states in fiscal 1997 and which regions of the country should get those dollars.

Warner charged that S. 672, the Supplemental Appriations Bill, includes $475 million in additional federal highway funding that the Senate Appropriations Committee has decided will go exclusively to states in the Northeast.
"Pro-northeastern forces" on the Senate Appropriations Committee inserted language that denies "donor" states access to supplemental highway funding, Warner said.
Under ISTEA, the Intermodal Surface Transportation Efficiency Act of 1991, "donor" states are those that send more federal gasoline tax revenue to Washington than they get in return.
Warner said he will introduce an amendment to strip the "unfair funding language" from the supplemental funding bill.
A spokesman for the Senate Appropriations Committee was unavailable for comment.
